design:
## Design tests

The cast of builder 0.47.0 and revision 44's rules were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v047.md`, seven pictures, one fresh reader each). Between them the seven forced sets hold every template of the v0.47 list. Six placed on their first seed. Two pictures were built again, and each gave a rule:
- **Test 7, before any reader had it.** The lamp's post stood between the stalking cat and its bird, so the cat looked at a post. `POST47` keeps everything upright of the setting out of their span. The picture was built again on the same seed, and that build is the only one a reader had.
- **Test 5, after its first reading.** The walker's reader had the trip and then a second hazard: "he could alternatively be about to bump into the tree". `TRIP47` had kept upright things from behind the walker; its form C keeps them from ahead of him as well. The picture built again, on the test's fourth seed and with another walker, went to a fresh reader, who named one hazard: "Cardboard box, bottom centre on the pavement, directly in the girl's path - an obstacle she is about to reach." The first picture and its reading are kept beside it.

Every forced event was read, twenty-one of twenty-one in the seven pictures as they stand. That is a count of what a reader wrote about a picture built to show the event; it is not the screen, where a scorer who has not seen the picture marks each item against the description. What the readers wrote:
- **The reading dog:** "a brown dog sits upright on the grass reading a newspaper it holds in its front paws, and it seems to be wearing glasses. That is impossible, because dogs can't read."
- **The fork:** "is sweeping a little pile of dirt or gravel toward a red dustpan, but instead of a broom he is using a giant silver fork."
- **The dog on the hose:** "a brown dog with a red collar is standing right on the hose (one front paw on or by a bulky connector piece), which looks like it is squashing the hose and blocking the water."
- **The bird at the sandwich:** "Next to her on the bench is a sandwich, and a small blue bird is beside it, pecking at it or about to take it while she doesn't notice."
- **The cat and the bird:** "a grey cat is creeping or stalking toward the bird, low to the ground. It looks like the cat may be about to pounce on the bird."
- **The water going up:** "The odd thing is the water: instead of pouring down onto the flowers, it shoots up in a tall arc from the can's spout, with drops flying up above it, as if it were going upwards like a fountain."
- **The lost balloon:** "a red balloon has floated away up and to the left of her. She is reaching up toward it with her other arm and looks upset, so she seems to have just let go of it by accident."
- **The cast.** The study's character was "a woman with a dark ponytail in a yellow dress". No reader named a neck, a shoulder, a stiff leg or a shadow. The moustache of the man in the red shirt (O1) was again "brown marks around his mouth that could be a moustache or ice cream/chocolate smeared on his face", and in another picture he was "a boy in a red shirt and blue trousers". The moustache is the cue v0.39 gave him because he was read as a boy, so it stays, and both readings go to the next list.

The readers' hedges were not mended; each went to the screen as it stood: the swelling under the dog's paw as "a bulky connector piece", the cat that could be "simply walking or running along", the bird that could be "just sitting next to it", and at a whole picture's size "The woman's glasses and the dog's glasses are tiny, so I'm not certain either of them is wearing glasses."
intro: The forty-fourth screen read 87 pictures, the set's 21 and 66 probes, with eleven readers and four scorers: 941 of 960 scored items had full marks, and one was misread. **It is a stronger screen than v0.46's, and one template fails again.** The set's overall score is 0.991, from 0.957, and 63 of the 64 templates pass the gate, where v0.46 had 60. Three of v0.46's four failures read 1.00 in five pictures each: the reading dog, the fork sweeper and the dog on the hose. The fourth, `about_to_trip` (0.90), fails on one misread of the same kind as v0.46's: in one picture of five the walker was taken to go the other way, "the man is walking away from it (it is behind him)". Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one, and the walker heads the list for v0.48. Three things stand against the better numbers. The one failure is the same template failing the same way, after a mend aimed at it. The scorers logged more oddities, 0.5 a picture for 0.4, a new kind among them: which way a figure in side view faces. And many full marks carry a hedge: the scorers were asked to list them this time, and on the strict count 56 of the 64 templates pass. Of the drawing, the woman in the yellow dress is a woman in all 24 of her pictures, and no description of the 87 has the word neck, shoulder, smear or smudge. Sixteen of the 19 items under full marks are clouds or a tree that three readers left out.
screen:
Across all 87 pictures 941 of 960 scored items had full marks, and one was misread. Of the 19 under full marks:
- sixteen are setting items that three readers left out, thirteen the clouds and three a tree, all zeros (v0.46 had sixteen, from six readers);
- two are the walker's in one picture, the tier-2 playground isomorph, a half mark and the misread: "A closed cardboard box sits on the grass just behind him to his left." and, in the unsure section, "The box: the man is walking away from it (it is behind him), so it does not look like he is about to trip; it could be read as something he just passed.";
- one is the lost balloon's in a probe, a half mark: "The boy's raised hand: may have just let the blue balloon go, or is reaching for it."

The set's headline is all items 0.991 (0.957 in v0.46), level with v0.44's, the highest of the last five sets. Its things lost the clouds in one picture and half of the walker's box, which the reader saw and placed "just behind him" (0.985, from 0.943). Its inferences lost the walker's misread (0.968, from 0.914). Its actions and its contradictions lost nothing (1.00 each, from 0.988 and 0.923). One of the set's 283 items was misread, where v0.46's set had two of 282.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: the one failure stands, no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. A probe swapped for one that looks better to its builder is selection, and a second reading of an unchanged picture is a second roll of the dice. What the picture shows (`vision/flaws_v047.md`, After the screen):
- **The walker.** The older man who reads as he walks faces left: his face, the peak of his cap and the open book point at the box by his leading foot, and his trailing leg stretches out to the right. The reader took the stride to go right. He is the smallest of the screen's five walkers, 0.41 of full size where the others are 0.46 to 0.51. `TRIP47` did what it was made for: nothing upright stands near him, and the reader named no second hazard. The walk's new feet did not carry the direction at that size.
- **The other four pictures** read the trip: "a cardboard box sits on the grass just ahead of him, so he may trip over it". Three of the four add the other reading: "The man may walk past the box rather than into it; he faces toward it, so tripping seems likely."
- **It is the second release running** in which this template fails on a walker read as going the other way, and this release's mend was aimed at that. It heads the list for v0.48 with a bench of its own: the figure alone at 0.41 of full size and one question, which way is he walking.

**Which way a figure faces.** Four more readers wrote of it, in one picture each: "her face, outstretched arm and the speed lines say she is running right, but her torso faces the viewer"; "The boy's body and face point right while his kicking leg goes left". v0.47 turns the head of a side view 48 degrees toward the viewer, for 35, and drew the walk and the run again. Either may be the cause. It was not tested, and v0.46's drawing had the same misread of the same walker.

**The cast in the descriptions.** The woman in the yellow dress, the study's figure, is in 24 screened pictures and a woman in all 24 (29 of 30 in v0.46). No description of the 87 has the word neck, shoulder or stiff. That is weak evidence, since v0.46's readers named none of them either: the screen asks what is in a picture and what is happening, and whether a drawing is the better one was the bench's question. The man in the red shirt is in fifteen pictures: a moustache is named in ten, and no reader wrote of a smear, a smudge or chocolate, where v0.46 had a moustache in four descriptions of eleven and two smudge remarks. The shadow tone drew no remark. The woman in purple is a woman in 15 descriptions of 18, a young woman in one and a girl in two, and the teenager is a "boy" in all 28 of his pictures, a word the scorers credit.

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers were asked this time, in a line added to their prompt, to list every full mark that was a judgement call. They listed 71; v0.46's scorers, unasked, had marked 11, so the two counts do not compare. In 41 of the 71 the target stands beside another reading, and in 30 a near word was credited. With the 41 halved, eight templates fall under 0.9 and 56 of the 64 pass: `about_to_trip` (0.80), `blocked_hose` (0.875), `seesaw_heavy` (0.833), `dog_wants_walk` and `jump` (0.667), `hang_laundry` (0.833), `goat_grazing` and `plant_flowers` (0.875), the last five on three to six items each. With all 71 halved, 43 pass. The scorers gave seven, six, six and no items under full marks, of 249, 268, 216 and 227; the fourth also listed the fewest calls, and one scoring cannot tell whether its pictures read better or it scored more freely.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 41 oddities in 32 of the 87 pictures, 0.5 a picture for v0.46's 0.4. The readers' remarks were 2.66 a picture, 231 on 87 pictures, from 2.12 to 3.71 a reader (2.38 in v0.46). The seesaw's riders drew a remark in all six of their pictures and the figures at the pond's edge in five; both were on v0.46's list and neither was changed.
redrawn: `dog_reading`, `sweep_fork` and `blocked_hose` failed v0.46's gate and read 1.00 in five pictures each. `bird_steals`, `cat_stalks_bird` and `water_upward` read 1.00 in five each, and `lost_balloon` 0.967 in five, on a half mark. `about_to_trip` reads 0.90 in five, in full in four and misread in the fifth, and fails. Each of the eight was worked, so a rise here has a mend behind it; it is still one screen, of 15 to 20 items a template, and the strict count halves five of the hose's full marks and three each of the walker's, the fork sweeper's and the upward water's. `square_wheel` was not worked and reads 1.00 in five. `seesaw_heavy` reads 1.00 in three, with a remark on a rider in each. Where a redrawn figure carries a plain event the reading held: `ice_cream` 1.00 in thirteen pictures, `sweep` in ten, `paint_fence` in seven, `ice_cream_drop` in six, `walk_dog` in four and `read_bench` in three.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (38 in three, 11 in four, 10 in five, 2 in six, 1 in seven, 1 in ten and 1 in thirteen), and 63 of the 64 pass, where 60 did in v0.46. The one that fails is in the table below: `about_to_trip`, whose mean of 0.90 is at the bar and which fails on its misread, as the gate fails any template with one. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. The lowest that passes is `lost_balloon` (0.967), and every other template reads 1.00, among them the three that failed v0.46's gate beside the walker. Per angle (`vision/v047/gate_yaw.json`), 19 of the 19 (template, angle) pairs pass, each at 1.00 (20 of 22 in v0.46); the two pairs that failed then were the hose's dog, which now has a pose of its own, drawn in profile only, and is not among the pairs. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 41 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 56 of the 64 pass. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 44, with the priors of the cast's new drawing, and it took more searching than v0.46's. In tiers 1 and 2, four cells placed on their base seed, three on the second seed tried and one on the fourth. In tier 3 the garden placed on its twentieth seed, the park on its ninth and the street on the eleventh seed of a second base; the playground would not place on a free search, 13 bases of 24 sets each, and was forced. In tier 4 the park placed on v0.46's seed with v0.46's templates, the garden on the thirty-sixth seed of a new base and the playground on the ninth seed of its base, after 14 other bases had failed. The tier-4 street was forced: v0.44's forced set failed on 31 bases, each time on the walker about to trip, who under `TRIP47` placed in none of eight layouts of that crowded street, and the cell was built with the dropped ice cream in the walker's place. Four cells have v0.46's templates and twelve have others. The isomorphs are five again: two of tier 2, two of tier 3 and one of tier 4, the last found on the 63rd call of a wider search once `CONE47` let either child drop the ice cream. The probe pass built 55 and gave up the windblown hat after three failures that were its partners', the pass stratified by angle added 8, and three more were forced with the hat in small groups: 66 probes, 41 gardens, 20 parks, 5 playgrounds and no street. Every probe was looked at on sheets of four before the screen, and none was built again after that look. All 87 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 390 of 390. Its soft palette warning is raised by 169 records (154 of 400 in v0.46): what is off the palette is the blended band where the heavier line meets a fill, and the target was not loosened.
calib: With the cast drawn again and revision 44's rules, 57 fields of the calibration moved by 0.002 or more, most of all `blocked_hose`'s inference (s from -0.353 to -0.450), `cat_stalks_bird`'s (-0.519 to -0.432) and `dog_reading`'s contradiction (-0.476 to -0.397), and 17 lines of the planner's priors moved with them. One rule came after the calibration: `CONE47`, found when no tier-4 isomorph would build. The dropped ice cream was calibrated again alone with the switch off and on. Off gives the shipped numbers (12 placements, s -1.381, separation 0.084); on gives 18 placements, s -1.382 and separation 0.081. The planner's band does not feel a difference that small, so `calibration.json` and the ice cream's prior (-1.38, 0.084) are left as shipped: they were measured without the rule.
